subject: MAP: throughput economics — tokens/$, batching & cache gating
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma@lumenai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: throughput economics — tokens/$, batching & cache gating

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our mutual action plan we need a short, verifiable cost/ops checklist to unblock procurement and finalize the pilot PO. I attached an initial throughput model (spreadsheet) and a one-page MAP execution timeline. Can your team confirm the three core inputs below so we can lock assumptions for the trial pricing: 

- Average tokens per request (input + response) — current working assumption: 420 tokens
- Target p95 latency SLO for interactive flows — 350ms
- Expected steady-state concurrency (RPS) for pilot peak — 18 RPS

Operational assumptions we used in the model (please flag if any are untenable):
- Batching: continuous batching window = 20ms; permissive batching allowed for non-interactive endpoints
- KV/prefix caching: 60s TTL for prompt/template cache; 95% cache hit rate assumed for templated responses
- Quantization: model will run int8; we budget a 6% quality delta allowance in eval plan

Deliverables and gating for MAP acceptance:
1) Evaluation plan (week 1): quantitative eval set (1000 prompts), pass threshold = top-1 F1 >= 0.88 for NER-style tasks
2) Throughput run (week 2): synthetic replay at peak RPS to confirm p95 latency and GPU utilization
3) Cost verification (week 3): token-per-dollar sensitivity & billing stub review

Can you confirm the three inputs above and whether LumenAI legal needs additional contract language around cache retention? If we get confirmation today, we can lock pricing in the MPO and target a pilot kickoff 7/7.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attachment: throughput_model_v1.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)
Attachment: map-exec-timeline.md (Markdown, 4KB)

From: Emma Li <emma@lumenai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: LumenAI Sales <sales@lumenai.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: throughput economics — tokens/$, batching & cache gating

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers from our side after a rapid sync with infra and legal: 

- Avg tokens per request: our logs show ~390 tokens avg for current flows (range 220–870). We can target 400 for the pilot if that helps reconcile safety buffers.
- p95 latency SLO: 350ms is aggressive for our customers; we generally accept 450ms as a business compromise. Can Redwood share the latency vs. batching tradeoff chart?
- Steady-state concurrency: 18 RPS peak is realistic for the pilot; we’ll provision a safety buffer to 25 RPS for load tests.

Caching/legal: legal asked for a short clause clarifying retention and access — they want to ensure cached prefixes are not considered persistent customer data beyond the TTL. I’ll send suggested language in a follow-up.

We reviewed your spreadsheet quickly; curious about the 20ms batching window — internal infra says their average request interarrival is bursty; if Redwood’s runtime requires 20ms to hit the token-per-dollar assumptions, we’ll need to validate that under our traffic pattern.

I’ll confirm final numbers by EOD after I run a quick telemetry sample and loop in our security lead if needed.

—Emma
PM, LumenAI

Emma —

Thanks — updated notes below after a quick sync w/ Karthik and Dylan. We can run two short validation artifacts in the pilot to de-risk the batching/cost assumption: 

1) Telemetry replay (run during week 2 throughput test): replay a 24-hour window of production traffic (anonymized) to measure realized batching hit rate and effective tokens/second. Owner: Dylan (redwood).
2) Micro-batching sensitivity sweep: test batching windows = [5ms, 10ms, 20ms, 50ms] and report tokens/$, latency p95, and GPU occupancy. Owner: Karthik (redwood).

Revised working assumptions for the MAP pricing sheet (we’ll update the attachment and the shared sheet):
- Avg tokens/request for billing: 400 tokens (adjusted per Emma’s note)
- Pilot latency target (soft): p95 <= 450ms; hard SLO for production to be agreed later
- Pilot peak concurrency for test scoping: 25 RPS (includes safety buffer)
- Cache TTL: keep as 60s in pilot; legal language fine to clarify non-persistent cache

Action items and dates (mutual):
- 6/30 EOD: LumenAI confirms final avg tokens and legal clause (Emma)
- 7/2: Redwood provides updated throughput_model_v2.xlsx and test scripts (Marissa/Karthik)
- 7/6: Telemetry replay + micro-batching sweep complete; results uploaded to shared sheet (Dylan)
- 7/7: Pilot kickoff (if gating metrics pass)

If that timeline looks good I’ll update the MAP doc and MPO. If Lumen needs a separate clause for cache access logs, call that out and we’ll coordinate with Security.

Best —
Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP: throughput economics — tokens/$, batching & cache gating

Quick technical note / confirmation from infra: 

- Micro-batching windows: our runtime can sweep the windows listed without deploy hours; 5ms will likely yield lower effective batching for small bursts, 20ms is where we typically see high token-per-dollar gains for bursty conversational workloads.
- Tradeoffs to watch: higher batching -> better tokens/$ but worse p95 tail; we will publish latency vs tokens-per-dollar table after the sweep.
- Cache hit sensitivity: if Lumen’s cacheable fraction is <60% the cost delta could be ~12–18% higher than the model. Dylan’s telemetry replay will quantify this.

I’ll own the micro-batching sweep and upload results into the shared sheet by 7/6. If legal sends cache clause language, forward it to infra-security and I’ll confirm no infra-level blocking concerns.

Karthik
Staff SW Eng, Redwood Inference
